newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BEVAN PRESSES CLAIM FOR TEST SPOT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEVAN PRESSES CLAIM FOR TEST SPOT.

text.p: Michael Bevan pressed his claim for
a place in Australia's test side to face West Indies with a
stylish unbeaten 58 as New South Wales took command of their
Sheffield Shield match against Victoria on Saturday.
Bevan, one of the candidates to fill the number three
position vacated by David Boon's retirement, guided his team to
174 for four in their second innings, a lead of 277.
In Brisbane, Queensland routed Tasmania by nine wickets.
Resuming at one for no wicket requiring a further 100 runs, the
home side cruised to victory with opener Trevor Barsby hitting
an unbeaten 48.
Bevan, who scored 79 in the first innings, was supported by
Michael Slater, another batsman keen to impress the selectors
ahead of the first test starting in Brisbane on November 22.
Slater made a typically brisk 69 to compensate for the
failures of Australia test captain Mark Taylor and all-rounder
Steve Waugh, who both fell cheaply.
Victoria captain Shane Warne, who is battling to prove his
fitness for test duty after finger surgery in May, bowled 10
wicketless overs at a cost of 29 runs.
Earlier, fast bowler Anthony Stuart claimed a first-class
career-best five for 63 as Victoria tumbled to 161 all out in
their first innings.
